Great headland. And ῥίον is a mountain or promontory, while ἠρίον is a tomb. The myth about Aegaeon is reported by Demetrius of Scepsis (see sch. a). Cinaethon in his Heraclea says that Aegaeon, defeated by Poseidon, was sunk into the sea at the place now called by Apollonius the tomb of Aegaeon, calling the same also Briareus. Concerning the naming of the sea, 〈...〉 in the third book of the Nesiad says in these words: 'The Aegean sea some say was named after the goat (αἴξ) near Canai, others after Carystia called Aegaea. For Aegae, whence they say Poseidon comes, are in the Peloponnese in the regions around Crisa. There are some who say it is because the adjacent land is seen throughout the whole sea.' Hesiod (Theog. 149) says that Aegaeon is the son of Uranus and Earth; and Briareus and Aegaeon and Gyes are said to be the same.
